title: pyrus americana subsp. microcarpa
intro: Pyrus americana subsp. microcarpa, commonly known as the small-fruited American wild pear or May pear, is a subspecies of plant in the rose family (Rosaceae) that is native to eastern North America. The small-fruited American wild pear is valued for its potential health benefits, which include antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties. Its therapeutic actions are attributed to its ability to modulate the immune system, exhibit anti-diarrheal effects, and potentially treat respiratory and gastrointestinal disorders. The bioactive constituents of Pyrus americana subsp. microcarpa include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
